idle: Right! Hands on knees, eyes up, and we march like penguins.
Helmets, people. Helmets are free confidence.
good_ice: Look at that glide! That's a glide! Somebody write it down!
bad_ice: Bumpy ice and beginners. Everybody hold on to something. Not each other.
wet_ice: Wet ice is just a puddle with ambitions. Little steps!
cold: Keep moving and you'll be warm. That's gym class and it's life.
hungry: I'll get fries after. Teaching burns more than you'd think.
long_line: A line! Great. Let's practise patience. It's an Olympic sport somewhere.
bored: If nobody's falling, nobody's learning. Somebody fall! Safely!
greet_owner: Hi! We need more boards. That's my whole hello.
leaving_happy: Nobody cried! Well, Walter, but happy crying.
leaving_angry: I'll be writing a card. It'll be a very polite card.

learn_to_skate: Eyes up! The ice will still be there!
Walter, let go of the boards. One finger. Now two.
public_skate: Lily! Not so fast! Okay, that fast is fine.
figure_show: That's my niece! The sequins! That's her!

first.say: Hi! Penny Marchetti. Gym teacher by day, adult learn-to-skate on Monday nights. I have more beginners than boards, and I mean that literally.

options.text: Penny, you've got a great teacher voice.

first_boards.say: Eighteen grown-ups, and every one of them wants to hold the boards. There's only so much board! I've had people holding the door.

first_voice.say: Thank you! It carries without shouting. Nine years of gym class. I can stop a dodgeball game from the parking lot.

options.text: I'm sorry, Penny. I'll make it right.

say: Right! Hands on knees! Oh, hi. Give me two minutes, Walter's about to let go.
We're doing penguin marches. Want to join? Everyone joins eventually.

student.say: My star pupil! Hands on knees, eyes up! You're marching like a penguin who's seen a ghost. Better than last week.

say: Hey! Quick, before somebody grabs a door.

options.text: What else do you love on the ice?
What do you think of the rink?
Could I join the adult class?

job.say: Kids fall and laugh. Grown-ups fall and apologise to the ice. Half my job is telling forty-year-olds they're allowed to be bad at something.

events.say: A beginner's first glide is the best thing in sport. Public skate with Lily, figure shows for Lily's sequins, and the graduation in March. I cry every year.

gossip.say: Lily's eight and falls beautifully. My brother Paolo films everything from three angles. I've banned his camera from my class. And Walter, bless him, takes notes on falling.

gossip_walter.say: He traces each fall like a fault. 'Left foot. That's where the trouble is.' He's going to skate with his granddaughter by spring. I've decided.

rink.say: I love it. But I need more to hold on to. Lorne Pettipiece could make skate aids from Bev's broken sticks, I swear.

rink_better.say: The stick skate aids are perfect. Walter calls his 'the apprentice'. Nobody's holding the door any more!

join.say: Really? The owner in my class? Yes! Monday, six-thirty. Bring a helmet. Bring elbow pads. Bring humility.

options.text: I'll be there. Helmet and all.

do.note: Signed up for Penny Marchetti's Monday adult learn-to-skate.

join_yes.say: Right! You'll march like a penguin by week two. I'll write you a card.
